style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The creation psalm of the word: by the word of the LORD the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath of His mouth -- He spoke, and it was; He commanded, and it stood. It has no title, and it may be the continuation of Psalm 32, whose closing call to rejoice it picks up and answers with a full orchestra: lyre, ten-stringed lute, a new song played skillfully. Its argument runs from the word to the world: God's word is straight and His work is faithful; He loves justice, and the earth is full of His covenant love. He gathers the sea in a heap and stores the deep like grain; He annuls the nations' plans while His own counsel stands from generation to generation. Then providence's eyes: He looks from heaven, gazes from His throne, has shaped every heart and understands every deed. So no king is saved by an army and the horse is a lie as far as rescue goes, but the LORD's eye is on those who fear Him, to rescue from death and keep alive in famine. It ends in the first person, the congregation's own hope: our soul waits; He is our help and shield; let Your covenant love be on us, even as we have hoped in You. The Te Deum's closing versicles borrow that line, one step before its final petition from Psalm 31:1.

1.text: Ring out your joy in the LORD, you righteous! Praise is fitting for the upright.
1.amp: Rejoice [ranan -- ring out] in the LORD [YHWH], O ye righteous [tsaddiq]: for praise [tehillah] is comely [naveh -- fitting, becoming] for the upright [yashar].
1.notes: rannenu tsaddiqim ba-YHWH (H7442, H6662): the ringing cry, commanded of the righteous -- la-yesharim navah tehillah (H3477, H5000, H8416): praise FITS the upright, the way a garment fits; Psalm 147:1's naveh. Psalm 33 has no title: it may be the continuation of Psalm 32, whose last verse it echoes.

2.text: Give thanks to the LORD with the lyre; make music to Him on the ten-stringed lute.
2.amp: Praise [yadah -- give thanks] the LORD [YHWH] with harp [kinnor -- lyre]: sing [zamar -- make music] unto Him with the psaltery [nebel -- lute] and an instrument of ten strings [asor].
2.notes: hodu la-YHWH be-khinnor (H3034, H3658), be-nebel asor zammeru-lo (H5035, H6218, H2167): give thanks with the lyre, make music with the lute and ten-string -- the same instruments as Psalm 92:3. The orchestra assembles for a new song.

3.text: Sing Him a new song; play skillfully, with a shout of joy.
3.amp: Sing [shir] unto Him a new [chadash] song [shir]; play [nagan -- pluck the strings] skilfully [yatab -- do it well] with a loud noise [teruah -- a shout, a blast].
3.notes: shiru-lo shir chadash (H7891, H7892, H2319): the new song of Psalms 96, 98, 144, 149 -- hetivu naggen bi-teruah (H3190, H5059, H8643): play WELL, with a teruah, the trumpet-shout of the New Year and the coronation. The Psalter's plainest command to musical excellence: skill is part of worship.

4.text: For the word of the LORD is straight, and all His work is done in faithfulness.
4.amp: For the word [dabar] of the LORD [YHWH] is right [yashar -- straight, upright]; and all His works [maaseh] are done in truth [emunah -- faithfulness].
4.notes: ki-yashar debar-YHWH (H3477, H1697): His word is STRAIGHT -- the same yashar as the upright of verse 1; God's word and God's people share an adjective. ve-khol-maasehu be-emunah (H4639, H530): all His doing is in faithfulness. The reason for the new song is the reliability of the old word.

5.text: He loves righteousness and justice; the earth is full of the covenant love of the LORD.
5.amp: He loves [ahab] righteousness [tsedaqah] and judgment [mishpat -- justice]: the earth [eretz] is full [male] of the goodness ['mercy', chesed -- covenant love, the KJV margin] of the LORD [YHWH].
5.notes: ohev tsedaqah u-mishpat (H157, H6666, H4941): God LOVES righteousness and justice -- they are His delights, not only His decrees. chesed YHWH maleah ha-aretz (H2617, H4390, H776): the earth is FULL of His covenant love -- the margin has 'mercy'; the sense is that creation is saturated with it (cf. Psalm 119:64).

6.text: By the LORD's word the heavens were made, and the whole host of them by the breath from His mouth.
6.amp: By the word [dabar] of the LORD [YHWH] were the heavens [shamayim] made [asah]; and all the host [tsaba -- army] of them by the breath [ruach -- breath, spirit] of His mouth [peh].
6.notes: bi-debar YHWH shamayim naasu (H1697, H8064, H6213): the heavens made by a WORD -- Genesis 1's 'and God said' as doctrine -- u-be-ruach piv kol-tsebaam (H7307, H6310, H6635): all their host, the stars, by the breath of His mouth. Word and Breath: the church has heard the Son and the Spirit in this verse since the Fathers (cf. John 1:3).

7.text: He gathers the waters of the sea together like a heap; He puts the deeps away in storehouses.
7.amp: He gathers [kanas] the waters [mayim] of the sea [yam] together as an heap [ned]; He lays up [natan] the depth [tehom -- the deep, the abyss] in storehouses [otsar -- treasuries].
7.notes: kones ka-ned me ha-yam (H3664, H5067, H4325, H3220): the sea gathered like a ned, a heap -- the word for the Red Sea's standing walls (cf. Exodus 15:8) -- noten be-otsarot tehomot (H5414, H214, H8415): the tehom, the primeval deep of Genesis 1:2, put in storehouses like grain. The chaos-waters of pagan myth are God's inventory.

8.text: Let the whole earth fear the LORD; let everyone who lives in the world shrink back in awe of Him.
8.amp: Let all the earth [eretz] fear [yare] the LORD [YHWH]: let all the inhabitants [yashab] of the world [tebel] stand in awe [gur -- shrink back in dread] of Him.
8.notes: yireu me-YHWH kol-ha-aretz (H3372, H776): the whole earth told to fear -- mimmennu yaguru kol-yoshebe tebel (H1481, H3427, H8398): gur here is the shrinking-back kind of awe. The Creator of verses 6-7 is owed the reverence of everything He made.

9.text: For He spoke, and it was there; He gave the command, and it stood firm.
9.amp: For He spoke [amar], and it was done; He commanded [tsavah], and it stood fast [amad].
9.notes: ki hu amar va-yehi (H559): He said, and it WAS -- Genesis 1's refrain compressed to two words -- hu-tsivvah va-yaamod (H6680, H5975): He commanded, and it stood. Creation by fiat: no struggle, no material, no delay. Psalm 148:5 says the same.

10.text: The LORD breaks up the counsel of the nations; He frustrates the plans of the peoples.
10.amp: The LORD [YHWH] brings ['maketh frustrate', pur -- a by-form of parar: breaks, annuls, the KJV margin] the counsel [etsah] of the heathen [goy] to nought: He makes the devices [machashabah -- plans, schemes] of the people [am] of none effect [nu -- forbids, thwarts].
10.notes: YHWH hephir atsat-goyim (H6331, H6098, H1471): hephir -- filed under pur (H6331) in Strong's but a by-form of parar, the annulling-verb used for breaking a vow (Numbers 30:8) or a covenant (Genesis 17:14) -- the nations' strategy annulled. heni machshevot ammim (H5106, H4284, H5971): their schemes refused. The God who spoke the stars can veto a cabinet.

11.text: The LORD's counsel stands firm forever, the plans of His heart through every generation.
11.amp: The counsel [etsah] of the LORD [YHWH] stands [amad] for ever [olam], the thoughts [machashabah -- plans] of His heart [leb] to all generations ['to generation and generation', dor va-dor, the KJV margin].
11.notes: atsat YHWH le-olam taamod (H6098, H5769, H5975): the same amad as verse 9 -- what He created stood; what He plans stands. machshevot libbo le-dor va-dor (H4284, H3820, H1755): the plans of HIS heart, against the plans of the peoples (v. 10). Two sets of plans in two verses; one of them survives.

12.text: Oh the blessedness of the nation whose God is the LORD -- the people He has chosen to be His own inheritance!
12.amp: Blessed [esher] is the nation [goy] whose God [Elohim] is the LORD [YHWH]; and the people [am] whom He has chosen [bachar] for His own inheritance [nachalah].
12.notes: ashre ha-goy asher-YHWH Elohav (H835, H1471, H430, H3068): Psalm 144:15's beatitude ('happy is that people, whose God is the LORD'), here widened from am, people, to goy, nation -- ha-am bachar le-nachalah lo (H5971, H977, H5159): the people He chose as His OWN inheritance: Deuteronomy 32:9, 'the LORD's portion is His people'. Election stated as God's inheritance, not Israel's.

13.text: The LORD looks down from heaven; He sees every one of the sons of men.
13.amp: The LORD [YHWH] looks [nabat] from heaven [shamayim]; He beholds [raah] all the sons [ben] of men [adam].
13.notes: mi-shamayim hibbit YHWH (H8064, H5027): the scene of Psalm 14:2 (there with shaqaph, 'looked down'); Psalm 102:19 has this same hibbit from heaven -- raah et-kol-bene ha-adam (H7200, H1121, H120): He sees ALL of Adam's sons. Verses 13-15 are the doctrine of providence's eyes: nothing human is off-screen.

14.text: From the place where He sits enthroned He gazes out on all who dwell on the earth --
14.amp: From the place [makon -- the fixed place] of His habitation [yashab -- His sitting, His throne] He looks [shagach -- gazes intently] upon all the inhabitants [yashab] of the earth [eretz].
14.notes: mi-mekhon-shivto hishgiach (H4349, H3427, H7688): from the makon, the established place of His session -- the throne -- He hishgiach, gazes with attention, the verb Song of Songs 2:9 uses for the beloved peering in at the windows. el kol-yoshebe ha-aretz (H776): at everyone who lives on the earth.

15.text: He who shapes the hearts of them all, who understands everything they do.
15.amp: He fashions [yatsar -- forms, like a potter] their hearts [leb] alike [yachad -- all together]; He considers [bin -- discerns] all their works [maaseh].
15.notes: ha-yotser yachad libbam (H3335, H3162, H3820): the potter-verb of Genesis 2:7, applied to every heart at once -- He formed them all, so He reads them all: ha-mebin el-kol-maasehem (H995, H4639). The Maker of the instrument understands its every note.

16.text: No king is saved by the size of his army; no warrior is delivered by great strength.
16.amp: There is no king [melek] saved [yasha] by the multitude [rob] of an host [chayil -- army]: a mighty man [gibbor -- warrior] is not delivered [natsal] by much [rob] strength [koach].
16.notes: en-ha-melekh nosha be-rob-chayil (H4428, H3467, H7230, H2428): the king not saved by the size of the force -- gibbor lo-yinnatsel be-rob-koach (H1368, H5337, H3581): the warrior not delivered by the size of his strength. rob twice: 'much' is the false god of the verse. Psalm 20:7's chariots and horses, spelled out.

17.text: The horse is a false hope for rescue; for all its great strength it cannot pull anyone out.
17.amp: An horse [sus] is a vain thing [sheqer -- a lie, a false hope] for safety [teshuah -- rescue, victory]: neither shall he deliver [malat -- let escape] any by his great [rob] strength [chayil].
17.notes: sheqer ha-sus li-teshuah (H8267, H5483, H8668): the horse is a LIE as far as rescue goes -- the finest military asset of the age called a falsehood -- u-be-rob chelo lo yemallet (H7230, H2428, H4422): its great strength lets no one escape. Third rob in two verses.

18.text: But look -- the eye of the LORD is on those who fear Him, on those who wait in hope for His covenant love,
18.amp: Behold, the eye [ayin] of the LORD [YHWH] is upon them that fear [yare] Him, upon them that hope [yachal -- wait expectantly] in His mercy [chesed -- covenant love];
18.notes: hinneh en YHWH el-yereav (H5869, H3373): against the horse's strength, an EYE -- the LORD's, on the fearers -- la-meyachalim le-chasdo (H3176, H2617): on those waiting for His covenant love, the phrase of Psalm 147:11. Providence's gaze (vv. 13-15) narrows to a focus.

19.text: to rescue their soul from death and to keep them alive in famine.
19.amp: To deliver [natsal] their soul [nephesh] from death [mavet], and to keep them alive [chayah] in famine [raab].
19.notes: le-hatsil mi-mavet naphsham (H5337, H4194, H5315): the natsal, the snatching-out, that the warrior could not manage (v. 16) -- u-le-chayyotam ba-raab (H2421, H7458): and to keep them alive in famine, the slow death that armies cannot fight. The eye of verse 18 is a rescuing eye.

20.text: Our soul waits in longing for the LORD; He is our help and our shield.
20.amp: Our soul [nephesh] waits [chakah -- waits with longing] for the LORD [YHWH]: He is our help [ezer] and our shield [magen].
20.notes: naphshenu chikketah la-YHWH (H5315, H2442): chakah is the tarrying-wait, the word Isaiah 30:18 uses of God waiting to be gracious -- ezrenu u-maginnenu hu (H5828, H4043): help and shield, Psalm 115's refrain. The psalm turns from third person to first: 'we' have chosen the eye over the horse.

21.text: For in Him our heart rejoices, because we have put our trust in His holy name.
21.amp: For our heart [leb] shall rejoice [samach] in Him, because we have trusted [batach] in His holy [qodesh] name [shem].
21.notes: ki-bo yismach libbenu (H8055, H3820): joy located IN Him -- ki be-shem qodsho batachnu (H8034, H6944, H982): because in His holy Name we have trusted. Joy is downstream of trust, and trust has an object: the Name.

22.text: Let Your covenant love, O LORD, rest upon us, just as we have set our hope on You.
22.amp: Let Your mercy [chesed -- covenant love], O LORD [YHWH], be upon us, according as we hope [yachal] in You.
22.notes: yehi-chasdekha YHWH alenu (H2617, H3068): let Your chesed be over us -- ka-asher yichalnu lakh (H3176): even as we have hoped in You. Not a rate God is bound by -- hope earns nothing -- but the plea that His covenant love answer the expectation His own word has raised (cf. Psalm 119:49). The Te Deum's closing versicles quote this verse, one line before its final petition, which is taken from Psalm 31:1.
